touches.text: A ticket's code is a tool or machine; its life is data. All of its state is on disk, so anyone can instantiate it to talk to it, and any dialog is written to the relevant part of the ticket as it happens. To cross a gate the ticket asks that gate to queue it, sending only its fileref: devices/codemother/0/machines/<inspector>/queueme <fileref>. The gate instantiates the ticket from that fileref on its own side. A ticket instance then processes the pass or fail: on a pass it goes on to the next step, alerting the probes watching the gate (3.3.4.2); on a fail it asks design to queue it, the same way. Self-queuing is the abstract ticket's (3.3.2), so every kind inherits it and no caller queues a ticket on its behalf (Akien, same day: "that could be in the class, rather than the instance :) self queuing"). WHY: Akien, 2026-11-10: "now it has to send it's fileref over to the thing that will process it, and a new code instance created over there even tho it's the same thing... because that's good encapsulation. :)"
Two kinds of request: Send, asynchronous, like sending an email; and Show/Get, synchronous, like requesting a web page.

A shim waking its device never takes more than 60 s. A sync caller waits at most 60 s for the wake, then gets "not now" back; a wake that misses 60 s is a trouble. 600 s is the limit for an inference call to come back, not for a wake.

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
Runs a proof as its own process and writes a validation record (claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon).
A timed-out run is its own outcome, not red.
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

open_questions.text: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?
